headline: Vaccines teach your immune system to fight enemies it's never met
universal_truth: Preparation beats reaction; training before battle determines the outcome
fun_facts: Smallpox killed an estimated 500 million people in the 20th century alone—vaccines eliminated it entirely
Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine in 1796 using cowpox to prevent smallpox
Your immune system has memory cells that can remember threats for decades
discussion_questions: How is a vaccine different from medicine?
Why do some vaccines need boosters?
What diseases might we eliminate with vaccines in the future?

hook.script: Your immune system is smart—once it defeats an enemy, it remembers. Next time that enemy appears, it's destroyed before you even feel sick. Vaccines hack this system, introducing harmless versions of threats so your body learns to fight them in advance.

cliff.script: If vaccines contain parts of diseases, why don't they make you sick? How can introducing a threat train your immune system without causing the disease itself?
cliff.prompt: How do vaccines train without infecting?

options.text: They use weakened, killed, or partial versions of pathogens—enough to trigger learning without causing disease
options.response: Yes. Vaccines show your immune system what to fight without giving it a real battle. It's like training with a practice target instead of live ammunition.

options.text: Vaccines contain antibodies that do the fighting for you
options.response: That's a different treatment. Vaccines teach your body to make its own antibodies...

fact1.title: Immune Memory
fact1.script: Your immune system creates 'memory cells' after fighting infections. These cells remember specific enemies for years or decades. Vaccines trigger this memory creation without requiring you to suffer through the actual disease.

fact2.title: Smallpox Victory
fact2.script: Smallpox killed hundreds of millions. In 1796, Edward Jenner showed that cowpox infection prevented smallpox. By 1980, global vaccination had eliminated smallpox entirely. It's the only human disease we've completely eradicated.

fact3.title: Herd Protection
fact3.script: When enough people are vaccinated, diseases can't spread—even to those who can't be vaccinated. This 'herd immunity' protects entire communities. Individual vaccination is also collective protection.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Preparation beats reaction. Vaccines prove that training before battle determines outcomes. Your immune system is powerful, but it's even more powerful when it knows what's coming.

outro.script: That's Day 127. Tomorrow, we'll explore fixing the body from inside—surgery. Until then, appreciate that your immune system can learn—and that we've found ways to teach it.

growTrack.title: Immune Appreciation - Know Your Defenders
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate your immune system's learning ability
growTrack.activity: Consider which vaccinations you've had. Each one trained your immune system against a specific threat. Your body now has memory cells ready to fight enemies you've never actually encountered. Preparation is protection.
